title: docs(spec): server.trustProxy describe names all three client-address consumers
body:
Closes #25058

Clause-②: no (prose only: no shape, key, default or accepted value moves)

## What

The `server.trustProxy` `.describe()` and TSDoc in `packages/spec/src/system/stack-server.zod.ts` said the client-address rule had two consumers. There are three. The text now names the endpoint policy chain's per-endpoint rate limiter as well, and the generated row in `content/docs/references/system/stack-server.mdx` is regenerated from it (`gen:docs`, as `check:generated` named it stale). Prose only: `z.boolean().default(false)`, the strict object around it and every sibling key are unchanged. Changeset: `@objectstack/spec` `patch`.

## Every consumer, checked on `origin/main` (`ba244f1b48`, merged into this branch)

All three reach the one rule, `resolveClientAddress` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address.ts`), under the one authored `server.trustProxy` that `objectstack serve` reads at `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:4733` (dispatcher) and `:4263` (auth).

1. **Inbound rate limiter**: `packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.ts:156-159` (via `resolveRateLimitKey`, `:306-310`), installed at `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts:906-908`. It is `null`, so nothing is registered, unless a budget is declared and enabled. That matches the qualifier "when `server.security.rateLimit.enabled` is set".
2. **Endpoint policy chain**: `packages/runtime/src/endpoint-policy.ts:366-372` calls `resolveRateLimitKey` with `trustProxy: input.trustProxy === true` whenever `limiters.limiterFor(endpoint)` returns a limiter, and that happens only when the endpoint's own `rateLimit` is enabled (`deriveBucketConfig`, `:162-174`). The value is threaded at `dispatcher-plugin.ts:2278-2282`. The registry is built unconditionally at `dispatcher-plugin.ts:2115`, so this limiter does not depend on the server-level budget. That matches the qualifier "whether or not the server-level one is".
3. **`AuthPlugin`**: `AuthManager.resolveClientAddress` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts:10059-10066`), used by the D5 allow-list (`auth-plugin.ts:2777-2784`) and the D7 `last_login_ip` stamp.

**No fourth.** `git grep` over the whole tree, excluding tests, for `resolveClientAddress`, `resolveRateLimitKey` and `trustProxy` finds no other caller. The other uses (`client-address-forwarding.ts`, `client-address-vendor.ts`, `request-client-address.ts`) are internal to `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, which means they fall under consumer 3.
